c.tagline: Central Asia's ancient Silk Road capital, reborn modern.

taxi.fareNote: Street taxis usually negotiate a fixed price before departure; ride-hailing apps like Yandex Go show an upfront fare and are the more reliable, safer option.

emergency.note: Unified mobile emergency number 112 also works; fire brigade is 101.

avoid.reason: Watch for taxi overcharging and petty theft at Chorsu Bazaar, and carry your passport as police document checks occur.

hood_desc: The modern, business-oriented heart of the city around Amir Timur Square, packed with international hotels, government buildings, and museums; ideal for first-time visitors who want everything within walking distance.
A leafy, upscale district of wide avenues, shopping malls, and the striking blue-domed Minor Mosque; suits travelers who prefer a quieter, more residential base with easy metro access.
The atmospheric Old City around Chorsu Bazaar, with narrow lanes, madrasas, and the vast domed market; best for travelers chasing an authentic, traditional Uzbek atmosphere.
A green, academic and diplomatic quarter served by its own metro stop, home to embassies and the national university; good for a calmer stay still close to the center.
A central, well-connected residential district near the main railway station, favored by budget travelers and longer-stay visitors for its guesthouses and value hotels.
lodging: Holiday Inn Tashkent City by IHG

water.note: Avoid tap water; stick to bottled or boiled water.

transit.pay: Metro and most city buses use the contactless ATTO smart card (also loadable with mobile wallets like Apple/Google Pay), tapped at turnstiles or validators; cash is still accepted for a single metro ride (3,000 som) at station counters. Tourists can buy an ATTO card at any metro station.
transit.hours: Metro operates roughly 5:00-24:00 daily; buses run similar hours with reduced frequency late at night; no all-night service.
transit.note: The metro (opened 1977, the first in Central Asia) has 4 lines and is clean, cheap, and a tourist attraction in itself for its ornate Soviet-era stations.

train: Tashkent Railway Station (Afrosiyob high-speed trains to Samarkand/Bukhara, Sharq express trains)
bus: Intercity/regional buses from Tashkent bus terminals

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus (~40 min to center)

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving 5-10% in restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory; tipping taxi drivers is uncommon.
